result.markdown: --- title: "[calibrate_sigma()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-function}" body-classes: doc-api-page page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Find the ELF bandwidth sigma that minimises out-of-sample ELF loss. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/calibration.py#L13-L123){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python calibrate_sigma( formula, data, tau=0.5, *, n_folds=5, sigma_values=None, method="GCV", seed=None ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} The quantile family used by `QuantileGAM` and `GAM` with quantile loss replaces the non-differentiable check function with a smooth "extended log-F" (ELF) surrogate controlled by a bandwidth `sigma`. Too large a `sigma` over-smooths the check loss and biases the fitted quantile; too small a `sigma` makes the surrogate nearly non-differentiable again and can destabilize IRLS. `calibrate_sigma` selects `sigma` empirically by K-fold cross-validation: for each candidate value, the model is fit on `K - 1` folds, predictions are made on the held-out fold, and the true (non-smoothed) pinball loss $$\rho_\tau(y - \hat q_\tau) = (y - \hat q_\tau)\,(\tau - \mathbb{1}[y < \hat q_\tau])$$ is accumulated across folds. The sigma minimizing total out-of-sample pinball loss is refined with a second, finer grid search around the best value from the coarse grid. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [formula]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : GAM formula string, e.g. `"y ~ s(x)"`. [data]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [InputData]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Column-oriented data dict. [tau]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[0.5]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Target quantile level in `(0, 1)`. [n_folds]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[5]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Number of CV folds. [sigma_values]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray | list[float] | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Candidate sigma values to evaluate. If `None`, a log-spaced grid of 10 values from `0.01 * sd(y)` to `2 * sd(y)` is used, followed by a refinement grid around the best value. If an explicit grid is passed, no refinement step is performed. [method]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["GCV"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Smoothing parameter selection method used when fitting each candidate model (`"GCV"`, `"REML"`, `"ML"`). [seed]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Random seed for fold assignment. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Calibrated sigma value (the one minimizing CV pinball loss). ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} ::: {#67f39a11 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import numpy as np from whittaker.calibration import calibrate_sigma rng = np.random.default_rng(0) n = 400 x = rng.uniform(0, 1, n) y = np.sin(2 * np.pi * x) + rng.normal(scale=0.2 + 0.3 * x, size=n) best_sigma = calibrate_sigma("y ~ s(x)", {"x": x, "y": y}, tau=0.9, n_folds=5, seed=0) print(round(best_sigma, 4)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` 0.0143 ``` ::: :::
